To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a glycerol molecule binds to the active site of pig heart SCCT, causing a 13 degrees rotation of the previously undefined domains, which close around the substrate binding site.

the high-resolution structure of the enzyme pig heart SCOT reveals that the enzyme is composed of four identical subunits, that the structure shows the binding of a glycerol molecule in the active site of one of the subunits and that this binding is accompanied by a relative movement of two previously undefined enzyme domains.
the high resolution (1.5 A) crystal structure of pig heart enzyme reveals a previously undefined domain that closes around the active site during catalysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural and functional characterization of the enzyme succinyl CoA:3-ketoacid-CoA transferase (SCOOT) which plays a key role in the catabolic pathway of ketone bodies.
the study of the structural dynamics of SCOT, which is a key enzyme in ketone-body metabolism.
the structural and functional characterization of the enzyme succinylCoA:3- oxoacid coenzyme-A transferase (SCoT) and its role in the metabolism of the ketone bodies in tissues outside the liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the glycerol-binding site and the active site are not identical, but the binding of glycerols and acetoacetates is similar, and the binding of acetoacetates may be accompanied by a conformational change in the enzyme.

the structure of pig heart enzyme is not a good model of the native enzyme, and it is likely that the structure of a glycerol complex represents an enzyme-substrate complex, which is an important step in the mechanism of catalysis.
the structure of SCOT is now known at atomic resolution, and the binding orientation of acetoacetate is proposed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

this structure of pig heart enzyme is the highest resolution structure of a member of the SCOT enzyme family and the first structure to show a conformational change of the protein associated with a change in ligand binding.
the glycerol is a competitive inhibitor, which is bound at the active site and induces domain movements.
we have solved the crystal structure of a glycerol-bound form of pig heart SCCT and that the glycerol-binding is associated with a domain movement that closes around the substrate-binding sites.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SCOT is a dynamic enzyme, which is likely to undergo conformational changes in order to accommodate the binding and release of substrates and products.
the structure of the glycerol complex of pig heart SCOt provides a model for the binding of the cosubstrate acetoacetate.
glycerol binding in the active site of the enzyme induces a substantial relative movement of two domains that close around this site, and that this domain movement could be functionally important.
